question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}, & \,0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}{e}^{y}, & \,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡9, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 1,0\le Y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡9).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{8}{e}^{y} \\  & =\frac{3}{32}{e}^{y}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,2]\times [0,\operatorname{ln}⁡9].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{32}{e}^{y}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡9 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1,0\le Y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡9) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}\frac{3}{32}{e}^{y}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{32}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{x}^{3}}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}-0 \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
